testResults.name: capability-oriented-scaffold
testResults.result: The harness product root contains deliberate core, data, fills, OMS, portfolio, results, risk, runtime, strategy, testing, venues, and CLI capability facades; tests mirror the product structure

testResults.name: process-commands
testResults.result: The harness help lists all three planned process groups, standalone commands expose help, and unimplemented process launches fail explicitly instead of pretending to run

testResults.name: package-and-image-surface
testResults.result: The wheel contains both lake and harness packages and publishes lake, harness, api, backtest-job, and trader console scripts; the Docker builder asserts all five installed commands while preserving the deployed lake entrypoint

testResults.name: focused-tests-and-quality
commands: uv run ruff check src/harness tests/harness strategies
uv run ruff format --check src/harness tests/harness strategies
uv run ty check src/harness tests/harness strategies
testResults.result: 14 focused tests and all focused quality checks passed

testResults.name: deterministic-core-boundary
testResults.result: The scaffold introduces no synchronous engine implementation and no wall-clock, unseeded randomness, network, Azure, FastAPI, subprocess, or lake dependency in harness core capabilities

testResults.name: architecture-and-wave-integration
testResults.result: Repository architecture documents the harness product boundary and capability layout; the frozen wave passed all repository checks

decisions: Capability facades remain empty until later CLEO tasks establish stable public contracts.
The shared image retains ENTRYPOINT ["lake"] for deployed market-lake compatibility; harness process binaries are installed for explicit command overrides.
No strategy-facing contract or engine path exists in this scaffold, so no strategy contract migration or determinism golden update was required.
limitations: A local wheel build validated packaged commands; Docker was unavailable for a local image build.
Harness API, backtest, and trader launches are intentional placeholders owned by later tasks.
